skill.name: incident-runbook-templates
skill.description: Create structured incident response runbooks with step-by-step procedures, escalation paths, rollback actions, and communication templates.
skill.summary: Create incident response runbooks for outages, database issues, escalation, recovery, and stakeholder updates.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All static findings are Markdown documentation examples in SKILL.md, not executable skill code. The shell, SQL, URL, CIDR, and /dev/null matches are runbook placeholders or manual commands, with no evidence of automatic execution, exfiltration, or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples can be mistaken for executable skill behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short operator-review warning before command sections and state that users must adapt commands to their environment.

remediation.issue: Placeholder URLs and CIDR ranges trigger network and IP scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Mark all URLs, service names, and CIDR ranges as examples, and instruct users to replace them with verified internal values.

content.value_statement: Incident teams need consistent procedures before outages occur. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft runbooks with triage, mitigation, rollback, escalation, and communication steps.
actual_capabilities: Defines severity levels, response times, and incident impact criteria.
Creates sections for detection, triage, mitigation, rollback, verification, escalation, and communication.
Provides service outage and database incident runbook structures.
Includes examples for health checks, deployment rollback, scaling, feature flags, and database checks.
Drafts internal incident notifications, status updates, and resolution messages.
limitations: Does not verify commands against a real production environment.
Does not execute incident response actions.
Requires teams to replace placeholder services, URLs, channels, and contacts.
Does not provide legal or compliance advice for regulated incidents.

use_cases.title: Standardize On-Call Response
use_cases.description: Create consistent runbooks for common service failures, escalation paths, and recovery checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare Service Recovery Steps
use_cases.description: Document service-specific triage, rollback, scaling, and verification procedures before incidents occur.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Incident Communications
use_cases.description: Draft internal updates, stakeholder notices, and resolution summaries that match incident severity.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an incident runbook for [service] with severity levels, alerts, triage steps, escalation contacts, rollback steps, and verification checks.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt an Existing Procedure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: convert notes into a template
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this incident procedure into a structured runbook for [team]. Include prerequisites, decision points, communication updates, recovery steps, and owner handoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Database Incident Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a database incident runbook for connection exhaustion, replication lag, and disk pressure. Include checks, mitigation choices, rollback guidance, and follow-up actions.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Runbook for Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this runbook for missing alerts, unclear escalation paths, unsafe commands, weak verification, and communication gaps. Return prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: Create a service outage runbook for a payments API.
output: A severity table with customer impact and response targets.
A triage flow covering alerts, dashboards, recent changes, and dependencies.
Mitigation and rollback sections with verification and communication checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Review our database incident steps for gaps.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review that flags missing prerequisites, unclear ownership, risky manual steps, weak rollback coverage, and incomplete recovery validation.

output_examples.input: Draft communication templates for a SEV2 incident.
output_examples.output: Initial, update, and resolution messages with severity, impact, status, actions taken, next steps, and owner fields.

best_practices: Replace every placeholder with current service ownership, dashboard, alert, and escalation data.
Test runbooks during drills before relying on them in production.
Keep rollback, verification, and communication steps close to each mitigation path.
anti_patterns: Publishing example commands before service owners review them.
Using generic escalation contacts that do not map to real responders.
Skipping verification steps after mitigation because metrics look improved.

faq.question: Does this skill execute incident commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates and example procedures. Operators must review and run any commands in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it help during an active incident?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft triage, mitigation, communication, and recovery checklists, but human incident leads should approve actions.

faq.question: Which teams benefit most?
faq.answer: SRE, platform, DevOps, security, and support teams can use it to standardize incident response documentation.

faq.question: Does it replace postmortems?
faq.answer: No. It can outline follow-up items, but teams still need evidence review, timelines, owners, and corrective actions.

faq.question: Can templates be customized for internal tools?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace placeholder services, dashboards, escalation channels, contacts, and health checks with approved internal values.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
